body:
Codex ADR review checkpoint: NOT ACCEPTED YET; please keep source beads closed. I found five blocking mismatches before the independent reviews return.

P0-1 identity: EmbedderInfo.info is static, but the proposed fingerprint includes per-request role, instruction, view, truncation, and dimension while one batch may vary them. Split static ProviderFingerprint from a validated EncodingRecipe or GeometrySpace identity; requests reference a recipe/space and results return its id. Query and Document compatibility needs an explicit GeometryId, not merely paired prose.

P0-2 result algebra: EmbedFailure.Abstained duplicates Estimate.Missing, and a PolicyDenied or preflight TooLong result cannot truthfully carry a ProviderCall because no provider was called. Separate execution failures from valid missing estimates and return an AttemptReceipt or batch receipt containing zero or more ProviderCalls plus policy/cache decisions. Require unique smart-constructed RequestIds.

P0-3 hard gate: L1 is not currently enforceable for every LocalCostModel. GraphHsmm trusts CostBreakdown.exclusion; a custom cost model or DefaultLocalCostModel(gating = false) bypasses it. Move admissibility into a separate typed gate/prepass, or confine no-gate behavior to an explicitly non-scientific ablation result type. Also the spike incorrectly requires context foils to be excluded; current code and tests deliberately keep ContextConflict aligned as a fidelity facet. Replace context rejection with context-mismatch detection and zero false gating.

P0-4 sensitive data: current Pseudonymized contains the reidentification key in the same value as the sanitized source. A RemoteCapability cannot safely bind to and pass that object. Split remote-safe PseudonymizedText from a separately held ReidentificationKey. Current ProviderCall and StageCacheKey use ordinary Checksum, so the ADR must specify a sensitivity-aware digest/receipt type rather than claiming HMAC through an unmarked Checksum. Key id, rotation, remote provider/model/purpose/expiry/budget, and no-echo errors belong in the capability contract.

P0-5 benchmark independence: a machine-built silver source model once M1 exists is circular if the tested embedding channel helped build it. Selection fixtures must be frozen independently of every tested channel. Ten percent audit is not enough for the held-out default-selection set, and generated silver cannot justify the word calibrated unless all scoring targets used for calibration are adjudicated.

I am continuing on cache key semantics, hierarchical metrics, structural segment coverage, and grakern laws. I will post one consolidated disposition after the two independent read-only reviews.
